name: Bollinger band reversion and squeeze breakout

origin.source_title: Bollinger on Bollinger Bands (McGraw-Hill, 2001); the bands were in use from the 1980s

how_it_works.simple: Draw a band two 'normal wiggles' above and below the 20-day average. Touching the bottom band means buy, touching the top means sell. When the band gets very narrow, wait for price to burst out and follow it.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a dog on a leash: most of the time it stays near you, but when it suddenly pulls hard after being still, it is usually chasing something.
how_it_works.precise: Middle band = SMA(20); upper and lower bands = SMA(20) plus or minus 2 rolling standard deviations. Reversion version: buy a close below the lower band, sell a close above the upper band, exit at the middle band. Squeeze version: when band width hits a multi-month low, trade in the direction of the first close outside the bands. Lento, Gradojevic and Wright (2007) test the reversion and contrarian forms.

rule: Daily: m = SMA20(close), s = 20-day standard deviation. Reversion: long when close < m - 2s, short when close > m + 2s, exit when close crosses m. Breakout: if (4s/m) is at a 120-day low, go long on the first close above m + 2s (short below m - 2s), exit on a close back through m.
economic_rationale: Reversion assumes short-term overreaction; the squeeze assumes calm periods are followed by large moves (volatility clustering). No risk premium is claimed.
why_it_might_fail: Lento, Gradojevic and Wright (2007) find the bands are 'consistently unable to earn profits in excess of the buy-and-hold' after costs, though a contrarian use did better. The two versions give opposite signals at the same band touch, so a trader can always find one that 'worked' in hindsight.

reported_results.source: Lento, Gradojevic and Wright (2007), Applied Financial Economics Letters, abstract
reported_results.market: Not stated in abstract (stock indices and an FX rate in the paper)
reported_results.notes: Abstract read through its OpenAlex record. After transaction costs the bands do not beat buy and hold; profitability 'is improved using a contrarian's approach'. No numbers in the abstract.

implementations.notes: Python wrapper for TA-Lib; has SMA, EMA, MACD, RSI, Bollinger bands and candlestick pattern functions.
Pure pandas indicator library, includes Ichimoku, Donchian channel, Bollinger, RSI, MACD.

relevance.reason: Simple to test on daily FX and SPY; the one academic test is negative after costs.
